question: During which of the following processes of the working of a bus AC system does the cool liquid through the expansion valve become gas and the gaseous refrigerant absorb a lot of heat energy?
solution:
The correct answer is __Evaporation**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Evaporation__ is the process during which the cool liquid refrigerant passing through the expansion valve becomes a gas.
 
• In this stage, the gaseous refrigerant absorbs a significant amount of heat energy from the surrounding air.
 
• This heat absorption leads to the cooling effect in the bus air conditioning system.
 
• Evaporation is a critical step in the refrigeration cycle and contributes to maintaining a comfortable temperature inside the bus.
 
• Other processes like compression, condensation, and throttling occur in different stages of the refrigeration cycle but do not involve the cooling liquid turning into gas and absorbing heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Throttling:**
 
 
• Throttling occurs when the refrigerant passes through the expansion valve, reducing pressure and temperature.
 
• It is a precursor to evaporation, setting up the conditions for heat absorption.
 
 
 
• **Compression:**
 
 
• The refrigerant gas is compressed to high pressure and temperature.
 
• Compression prepares the refrigerant for condensation by increasing its energy state.
 
 
 
• **Condensation:**
 
 
• Condensation occurs when the refrigerant releases heat energy and transitions from gas to liquid.
 
• This process takes place in the condenser coil.
